sentences.text:
Smt. Guddi Devi .....Applicant(s) Versus State of U.P. .....Opposite Party(s) Counsel for
Applicant(s) :
Ajay Kumar Yadav, Ray Sahab Yadav, Vijay Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party(s) :
Brajesh Kumar Singh, G.A. Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J. 1.
List has been revised.
Counter affidavit filed by learned counsel for the informant today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Vijay Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Brajesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 162 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Sirsaganj, District Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
She has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
The applicant is the mother-in-law of the deceased person.
5. Learned counsel has further stated that the applicant is languishing in jail since 08.04.2024 and she has been incarcerated for about one year and four months.
The trial is moving at snail's pace as only one witness has been examined to date.
There is no likelihood of early conclusion of trial in near future.
The applicant lives separately in another house.
6. The applicant has no criminal history.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, she will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.
7.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that smell of kerosene was present in the injury and it is not accidental injury and sofa etc. and other and other households were found intact as only deceased was found 94 % burnt.
There was hay found by which the deceased was burnt, as such the applicant is not entitled for bail.
8. This Court had called for a report regarding the status of trial and in compliance thereof, a report has been submitted by the Trial Court concerned dated 14.08.2025.

As per the said report, only one Smt. Guddi Devi vs State Of U.P. on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152741997/
1 witness has been examined to date.

sentences.text: 9. The Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.
It should also not be granted by looking into the discrepancies here or there in the deposition.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the applicant being mother-in-law and was available in the house on the said point of time and is one of the main accused, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
11. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

12. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

entities.text: Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

(Krishan Pahal,J.) September 2, 2025 Sumit S  Smt. Guddi Devi vs State Of U.P. on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152741997/
